s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic and laboratory evidence of myocardial injury, complicated by hypotension
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain with increasing intensity
ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG
Elevation of high-sensitive troponin T level
Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery on emergency angiography
key_facts: The patient is an older woman
The patient has a history of diabetes
The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain
The intensity of pain increased over time
Initial vital signs showed a normal heart rate and blood pressure
Blood pressure later fell to 60/40 mm Hg
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ECG showed subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
ECG showed downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
High-sensitive troponin T level was elevated at 0.309 ng/mL
Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic and laboratory evidence of myocardial injury, complicated by hypotension
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain with increasing intensity
ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG
Elevation of high-sensitive troponin T level
Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery on emergency angiography
key_facts: The patient is an older woman
The patient has a history of diabetes
The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain
The intensity of pain increased over time
Initial vital signs showed a normal heart rate and blood pressure
Blood pressure later fell to 60/40 mm Hg
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ECG showed subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
ECG showed downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
High-sensitive troponin T level was elevated at 0.309 ng/mL
Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed ST-segment elevation in multiple leads, including II, III, and aVF, and subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, which is consistent with an ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Additionally, the elevated high-sensitive troponin T level and emergency angiography showing thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: While the patient did have a myocardial infarction, the specific type is better described as ST-elevation myocardial infarction due to the ECG findings.

rejected.label: Cardiogenic shock
rejected.why: Although the patient's blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg, this is a consequence of the myocardial infarction rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's angina
rejected.why: Prinzmetal's angina typically presents with transient ST-segment elevation during episodes of chest pain, but the patient's ECG showed persistent ST-segment elevation and the angiography revealed thrombotic occlusion.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: While the computer tomography angiography revealed pericardial effusion, there is no indication of equalization of diastolic pressures or other signs of cardiac tamponade.
